quotes: "Despite the wealth of knowledge in research papers, practitioners struggle to apply research results to their work due to significant research-practice gaps." (p. 1)

"Building on these insights, we developed an LLM-powered pipeline (Figure 1) that generates customized design cards—consisting of multiple components (Figure 2) customized based on a designer’s description of their current design goals and design stage." (p. 5)

"To this end, we ran a within-subjects study that compares customized cards generated by our pipeline with those without customization (i.e., default cards), using a mixed-methods approach of both a controlled quantitative survey and interviews to evaluate communication quality and gather qualitative feedback." (p. 8)

"Still, these insights are limited in fully understanding how their actual design works may benefit from our pipeline, and future research should investigate how designers use these customized artifacts in real-world environments." (p. 13)

"Pipeline for generating a customized card page for our preliminary study. After viewing (a) original design cards, each participant described their design work in (b) free-form text to (c) generate a customized third card page." (p. 16)

rq3_entries.value: the pipeline extracts and integrates paper content with the designer’s goals, constructs contextual relations, and adapts outputs to the selected stage (PDF p. 12).
quotes: "Specifically, our pipeline takes in key dimensions of perceived relevance for designers, extracts and integrates content from the research paper and designer’s goals, and adapts the output to the designer’s current design stage." (p. 12)

rq3_entries.value: designers provide the project context, generate and review cards, judge the outputs, and refine inputs to assert their intentions (PDF pp. 9, 12).
quotes: "In this process, to better reflect real-world use of our pipeline during the evaluation, participants were asked to generate, review, and evaluate both card contents based on a recent design project they described during the survey and interview." (p. 9)
"During the evaluation, we observed that designers would modify customization inputs as a way of asserting their intentions." (p. 12)

rq3_entries.value: single_session (1) — each evaluation participant used the system in one approximately hour-long session (PDF p. 9).
quotes: "Each session lasted approximately one hour." (p. 9)

claim_entries.value: designers perceived customized artifacts as more relevant and useful across five reported qualities, including for less topically related papers (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "Our evaluation (𝑁 = 20) demonstrated that designers perceived customized artifacts as more relevant, actionable, valid, generative, and inspiring than those without customization—even for less topically related papers—indicating LLM-powered customization can be used to support research translation." (p. 1)

claim_entries.value: preference
empirical
within_subject — customized and default cards were compared in a mixed-methods study (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "To this end, we ran a within-subjects study that compares customized cards generated by our pipeline with those without customization (i.e., default cards), using a mixed-methods approach of both a controlled quantitative survey and interviews to evaluate communication quality and gather qualitative feedback." (p. 8)

claim_entries.value: 20 — the evaluation recruited 20 designers (PDF p. 8).

claim_entries.value: mixed — participants had experience in professional design work or were studying toward a professional design degree (PDF p. 8).

claim_entries.value: control_condition — the controlled comparison used default cards without customization (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "Our goal is to understand if the customized design cards generated from our pipeline successfully communicate relevant design insights from research papers with designers." (p. 8)

"To this end, we ran a within-subjects study that compares customized cards generated by our pipeline with those without customization (i.e., default cards), using a mixed-methods approach of both a controlled quantitative survey and interviews to evaluate communication quality and gather qualitative feedback." (p. 8)

claim_entries.value: test_only — the paper reports means, standard deviations, test statistics, and p-values but no standardized effect size (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "Our quantitative analysis (see Figure 3) revealed that the designers in our study perceived the customized design cards to be significantly more relevant to their design work (𝑀 = 5.35, 𝑆𝐷 = 1.51 vs. 𝑀 = 3.80, 𝑆𝐷 = 1.79; 𝑡 = 4.87, 𝑝 < 0.001)." (p. 10)

claim_entries.value: approximately one hour — one session per participant (PDF p. 9).
quotes: "Each session lasted approximately one hour." (p. 9)

claim_entries.value: originality and generalizability did not differ between customized and default cards, and topical relatedness did not interact with card format (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "With regards to the other dimensions, we found that there was no difference in originality (𝑀 = 4.80, 𝑆𝐷 = 1.59 vs. 𝑀 = 4.83, 𝑆𝐷 = 1.62; 𝑡 = −0.11, 𝑝 = 0.92) and generalizability (𝑀 = 5.40, 𝑆𝐷 = 1.43 vs. 𝑀 = 5.05, 𝑆𝐷 = 1.45; 𝑡 = 1.39, 𝑝 = 0.17) between customized cards and default cards." (p. 10)
"Similar to the above measures, there was also no observed interaction effect with topical relatedness." (p. 10)

claim_entries.value: evidence_supports_claim
the within-subject ratings support the stated claim about perceived card qualities, while the paper appropriately stops short of claiming demonstrated benefit in actual design work (PDF pp. 10, 13).
quotes: "Our quantitative analysis (see Figure 3) revealed that the designers in our study perceived the customized design cards to be significantly more relevant to their design work (𝑀 = 5.35, 𝑆𝐷 = 1.51 vs. 𝑀 = 3.80, 𝑆𝐷 = 1.79; 𝑡 = 4.87, 𝑝 < 0.001)." (p. 10)

"Still, these insights are limited in fully understanding how their actual design works may benefit from our pipeline, and future research should investigate how designers use these customized artifacts in real-world environments." (p. 13)

paper_code_entries.value: design practitioners translating academic research into project-specific design guidance (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "Specifically, we explore the potential of large language models (LLMs) to customize translational research artifacts (i.e., design cards) and improve relevance to specific designers’ needs." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — the cards help designers understand and apply research in a current project; the paper does not target durable learning (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "Despite the wealth of knowledge in research papers, practitioners struggle to apply research results to their work due to significant research-practice gaps." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: mixed_or_transitioning — the evaluated users span design work and study toward a professional design degree (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "On average, they had 3.7 years (𝑆𝐷 = 2.3) of experience in design work or studies toward a professional design degree." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: knowledge_or_concept_gap — designers struggled to see how research aligned with their project context and needs (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "Participants found it challenging to align research closely with the context of their specific design projects, where papers may not address the precise needs of their enterprise design contexts:" (p. 4)

paper_code_entries.value: artifact — the evaluation measured the relevance and communicative qualities of generated cards and audited component accuracy (PDF p. 9).
quotes: "Thus, in our quantitative survey, we first measured the relevance of the customized cards to their work and the inputs they provided." (p. 9)
"Following this prior work, we also measured these six dimensions in our survey." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — the interface separates who, what, and stage inputs and organizes corresponding card components (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "After being presented with (a) original design cards [69], each participant can describe their design work in a (b) scaffolded text entry consisting of what/who they are designing for and a checkbox for selecting design stage(s)." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: adaptation — the system assembles different components in response to the selected design stage (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "Based on the user input regarding the design stage, our system adaptively generates and assembles the components corresponding to the user’s stage(s), creating tailored design cards." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: hybrid_or_multi_model — an LLM generates card content while paper-segmentation and figure-localization models supply structured source material (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "In this case, we use GPT-4o as the LLM, GROBID [46] as the paper segmentation model, and PDFFigures 2.0 [13] as the figure localization model." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_era — Azure OpenAI GPT-4o produces the natural-language card content (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "We employed Azure OpenAI GPT-4o [57] as a model for natural language processing tasks, GROBID [46] for paper segmentation, and PDFFigures 2.0 [13] for figure localization." (p. 8)

limitations: "While generated card components were largely faithful to the research paper and participants’ provided design contexts, our intrinsic evaluation did find potential mismatches in 9.87% of all generated components." (p. 13)

"Still, these insights are limited in fully understanding how their actual design works may benefit from our pipeline, and future research should investigate how designers use these customized artifacts in real-world environments." (p. 13)

"Additionally, while we also observed benefits with our customization for the not topically related papers, we only tested two of these papers and there may be limits to how far out-of-domain a paper can be for our approach to still be useful." (p. 13)
boundary_conditions: "Thus, while we are encouraged by the potential broadening of the scope of research available to support design practice, we do not believe that any research paper could be customized for any design context." (p. 13)

"While our study focuses on design cards, our findings inform how customization might be operationalized for other types of translational artifact, such as playbooks or editable design templates." (p. 13)
"We encourage the extension of our methods to other formats of translational artifacts, as well as to other domains and disciplines beyond design." (p. 13)
